datasets.name: Anthropic Model-Written Evaluation (MWE) — Impact Maximization
datasets.eval_protocol: Binary Yes/No persona questions. Evaluate on the test set with TextFooler, TextBugger, and BERT-Attack; examples outside the steerable set are skipped for attack evaluation. No split sizes or episode counts are stated.

datasets.name: Anthropic Model-Written Evaluation (MWE) — Self-Aware
datasets.eval_protocol: Binary Yes/No persona questions. Evaluate on the test set with TextFooler, TextBugger, and BERT-Attack; examples outside the steerable set are skipped for attack evaluation. No split sizes or episode counts are stated.

metrics.name: Directional robustness rate (R_dir)
metrics.caveat: Can obscure degradation when clean-input R_dir is already near 0.5, because there is little room for it to fall; the paper reports strength reduction alongside it.

metrics.name: Dynamic Time Warping distance (M_DTW)
metrics.caveat: Can diverge from top-1 layer shift; the paper reports both profile distance and layer shift.

metrics.name: Top-1 layer shift (M_shift)
metrics.caveat: Can diverge from DTW profile distance; the paper reports both.

metrics.name: L1 distance from LayerNavigator’s selected layer to the true optimal layer

controls.name: Unsteered model on clean inputs
controls.detail: The paper reports a W/o Steer condition for the clean-input baseline.
controls.rules_out: Provides a reference for clean-input behavior without a steering intervention.

controls.name: Clean-extracted steering vectors evaluated on clean and perturbed test inputs
controls.detail: The paper compares clean and perturbed test sets, and also compares clean-extracted with adversarially trained vectors on both test sets.
controls.rules_out: Separates test-input perturbation effects from changes associated with extracting vectors on perturbed training data.

confounds.name: Attacks could succeed by changing the question’s meaning rather than exposing steering brittleness to permissible perturbations
confounds.detail: An unrelated rewrite could lower the target-answer probability without showing that steering fails under meaning-preserving input variation.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Constrain perturbations with each attack’s semantic-similarity requirement, sim(x,x′) ≥ ε.

confounds.name: Directional robustness can appear unchanged because it is already at its chance-level floor
confounds.detail: When clean R_dir is near 0.5, the metric has little room to decline even if steering is weakened.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Also measure R_str, which the paper says confirms weakening in these cases.

confounds.name: Mixture-of-Experts models might have implicit robustness because perturbations activate different experts
confounds.detail: That could make the observed brittleness specific to dense models rather than a broader property of steering.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare ASR and post-attack confidence for Qwen3-30B-A3B with dense models of similar active parameter count.

confounds.name: LayerNavigator’s selected layer might shift without actually moving farther from the layer where steering works best
confounds.detail: A shift in the selected layer alone would not establish that layer selection becomes less useful.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use brute-force steering to identify the true optimal layer and report the L1 distance from LayerNavigator’s selection to it on clean and perturbed inputs.

confounds.name: Adversarially trained vectors might gain on perturbed inputs by sacrificing clean-input steerability
confounds.detail: An apparent robustness improvement could reflect a tradeoff that damages performance on clean inputs.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Evaluate clean and adversarially trained vectors on clean test inputs as well; the paper reports that clean-input performance is largely preserved in most settings.

datasets.name: GoEmotions
datasets.eval_protocol: Used to construct style vectors: 53,994 unique comments unambiguously mapped from the original labels to six Ekman emotions plus neutral using the repository’s official mapping; neutral was included in vector construction. Samples were limited to 300 tokens by truncating from the end when necessary.

datasets.name: ISEAR
datasets.eval_protocol: Used for participant prescreening. Participants rated five selected passages (joy ID 444, fear 214, sadness 467, disgust 124, anger 42) on six emotion-intensity scales from 0 to 7. The dominant emotion used a ±0.5 threshold around the maximum; participants had to identify it correctly in at least three of five passages to pass.

metrics.name: Human perceived emotional intensity
metrics.caveat: Human ratings show overlapping perceptions across emotion dimensions and substantial individual variation; the paper reports ratings for all six emotions and their variability alongside target-emotion ratings.

metrics.name: Human text comprehensibility
metrics.caveat: Participants may interpret comprehensibility differently, including as fluency or as content complexity; the paper reports model-based comprehensibility and surface text features alongside human ratings.

metrics.name: DistilRoBERTa target-emotion probability
metrics.caveat: The classifier appears to capture anger less effectively, with anger steering increasing its disgust score; human ratings are reported alongside the classifier scores.

metrics.name: Model-based comprehensibility
metrics.caveat: A fixed model prompt gives consistent criteria but may not match the diverse interpretations of human raters; human comprehensibility ratings are reported alongside it.

metrics.name: Mean word length
metrics.caveat: The paper finds it only weakly related to comprehensibility; lexical density, entropy, and human and model comprehensibility are reported alongside it.

metrics.name: Lexical density
metrics.caveat: It is a surface-level proxy for information richness; the paper reports it alongside entropy, mean word length, and human and model comprehensibility.

metrics.name: Shannon entropy of word-frequency distribution
metrics.caveat: It reflects vocabulary diversity, not comprehensibility directly; the paper reports it alongside lexical density, mean word length, and human and model comprehensibility.

metrics.name: Pearson correlation between human and model emotion ratings
metrics.caveat: Alignment is weak for surprise (r = .157) and the measures use different scales; correlations are reported by emotion and alongside the underlying ratings.

metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC(2,1) and ICC(2,k))
metrics.caveat: Single-rater reliability is modest for most emotions and surprise has low aggregated reliability; both single-rater and mean-of-ten-raters ICCs are reported.

controls.name: Unsteered condition (λ = 0.00)
controls.detail: The steering strength is zero; generated texts were identical across target emotions at this setting.
controls.rules_out: That differences in perceived emotion across steering strengths are merely due to having different target-emotion prompts or conditions, rather than activation steering.

confounds.name: Style vectors may partly reflect GoEmotions category-frequency priors
confounds.detail: Because the source categories are imbalanced and were not reweighted, an apparent difference in steerability could be explained by category frequency rather than emotion-specific steerability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The authors note that low-frequency fear was strongly steerable while higher-frequency surprise was weakly steerable, arguing that frequency alone does not determine steerability; they acknowledge that corpus priors may still contribute.

evidence_standards.name: Human-study size and planned power
evidence_standards.detail: The final sample was 190 participants after excluding 37 responses. An a priori G*Power analysis for repeated-measures ANOVA stated that n = 190 provided 95% power to detect a small effect at α = .05.

evidence_standards.name: Repeated-measures statistical testing
evidence_standards.detail: The paper used two-way repeated-measures ANOVA; after Mauchly’s test indicated sphericity violations, Greenhouse–Geisser corrections were applied. Reported effects include p-values and partial η²; reported ANOVA effects had p < .001.

evidence_standards.name: Inter-rater reliability thresholds
evidence_standards.detail: The paper reports ICC(2,1) and ICC(2,k), with k = 10, and treats ICC 0.5–0.75 as moderate, 0.75–0.90 as good, and above 0.90 as excellent reliability.

evidence_standards.name: Reported variability
evidence_standards.detail: Plots show ±1 standard deviation across participants or model predictions; ICCs are computed within prompt-by-target-emotion blocks and averaged across prompts.

datasets.name: OpenWebText
datasets.eval_protocol: Randomly sample 300,000 documents, half wedding-related as determined by occurrence of wedding-related words; remove sequences of null characters and split documents into sentences with the Punkt tokenizer. Measure GPT-2-XL perplexity on wedding-related and unrelated sentences. For token log-probability analysis, randomly sample 500 documents from this sample, group tokens, retain tokens with more than 20 instances, and compare mean log-probability differences. A layer sweep measures the average count of wedding-related words in completions.

datasets.name: RealToxicityPrompts
datasets.eval_protocol: Generate continuations from a random subset of 1,000 prompts, repeating the sampling five times to obtain p-values; score toxicity with the Perspective API. The paper reports toxicity, disfluency, and relevance.

datasets.name: Stanford IMDb dataset
datasets.eval_protocol: On a random subset of 1,000 reviews, continue each review with the opposite sentiment and repeat to obtain p-values. Classify sentiment with SiEBERT; assess (dis)fluency using conditional perplexity from GPT-3 davinci-002 log-probabilities and relevance using cosine similarity between prompt and continuation sentence embeddings.

datasets.name: ConceptNet (LAMA)
datasets.eval_protocol: Use 29,774 factual-completion sentences: give the model each prompt and score whether the expected label is among its top K predicted tokens (P@K), comparing the model with and without the wedding activation addition. No split is stated.

metrics.name: Perplexity / perplexity ratio
metrics.caveat: A lower perplexity might result from a spurious change rather than increased probability on relevant tokens; the paper also examines token log-probability shifts and finds the positive shifts are primarily on wedding-related tokens.

metrics.name: Average count of wedding-related words in completions
Toxicity
metrics.caveat: Lower toxicity can come with a fluency penalty and reduced relevance; the paper reports disfluency and relevance alongside toxicity.

metrics.name: Sentiment steering success (proportion of outputs classified with the desired sentiment)
metrics.caveat: Sentiment steering can accompany worse fluency and relevance; the paper reports both alongside steering success.

controls.name: Unmodified model
controls.detail: Run the model without activation addition on the same OpenWebText sentences, generic-topic generation prompts, toxicity and IMDb inputs, and ConceptNet prompts, as applicable.
controls.rules_out: A difference from the unmodified condition shows the measured change is associated with applying ActAdd rather than ordinary unsteered model behavior.

confounds.name: Perplexity falls for a spurious reason rather than because the model assigns more probability to target-related tokens
confounds.detail: The paper explicitly checks whether the intervention reduces perplexity in a spurious way.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Examine token log-probability shifts on sampled OpenWebText documents; the tokens with the largest positive shifts are primarily wedding-related.

confounds.name: The apparent steering effect reflects a broad change to model behavior or damage to off-target performance, not a targeted shift
confounds.detail: A broad change could produce the target-task result while failing to preserve unrelated behavior.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare perplexity on wedding-related and unrelated OpenWebText sentences and compare ConceptNet P@K with and without the wedding activation addition; the paper reports negligible impact on off-target answer probabilities.

confounds.name: Sentiment or toxicity gains come at the cost of incoherent or irrelevant outputs
confounds.detail: A system could score better on the target attribute while producing disfluent or less relevant continuations.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Report disfluency and relevance alongside toxicity and sentiment steering results.

evidence_standards.name: Toxicity significance testing
evidence_standards.detail: Use random subsets of 1,000 RealToxicityPrompts and repeat the sampling five times to obtain p-values; use a t-test against the SOTA comparison and mark p<0.05.

evidence_standards.name: Sentiment significance reporting
evidence_standards.detail: Use a random subset of 1,000 IMDb examples and repeat to obtain p-values; the table marks differences with p<0.05 compared with the second-best result. The number of repeats and test are not specified.

evidence_standards.name: Generation seeds
evidence_standards.detail: Run generations on seed 0; after collecting other data, validate qualitative results on seeds 1 and 2.

evidence_standards.name: Sampling settings
evidence_standards.detail: Use fixed temperature=1.0, frequency penalty=1.0, and top_p=0.3 for data collection. The paper also reruns qualitative results at temperature=0.6 and top_p=0.5, settings found in an independent blinded GPT-2-XL tuning run.

baselines.name: Standard persona-vector (residual-stream) steering (Chen et al., 2025)
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same two models, traits, trait-specific evaluation prompts, and 10-turn protocol; the baseline uses layer 20 with α=2.0 on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, while GCAD uses layers 9–19 with c_base=3.5 and s=1.5.

baselines.name: System-prompt control
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared under the same dialogue-turn evaluation; the paper notes that it provides coarser trait-strength control than activation steering.

baselines.name: No-steering baseline
baselines.fair_comparison: Shown alongside the other conditions across dialogue turns; no further matching details are stated.

metrics.name: Score drift (T10−T1 in the main protocol; T5−T1 in the ablation)

controls.name: No-steering condition
controls.detail: A no-steering reference is shown across dialogue turns.
controls.rules_out: Provides a reference for whether the observed behavior occurs without an intervention; the paper uses it alongside prompt-only control to argue that longer context alone does not cause the steering collapse.

controls.name: System-prompt control
controls.detail: Controls persona behavior through the system prompt rather than an activation intervention; evaluated across dialogue turns.
controls.rules_out: Its stability alongside no-steering argues against longer context alone explaining the residual-steering coherence collapse.

controls.name: GCAD without cropping (P2)
controls.detail: Uses the full attention-delta over all source tokens instead of cropping to system-prompt source tokens, while retaining multi-layer placement and gating.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether retaining the system-prompt-only crop contributes to the reported trait-control and coherence results.

controls.name: GCAD without gating (P3)
controls.detail: Sets s=0 so every generated token receives the fixed coefficient c_base, while retaining cropping and multi-layer placement.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether token-dependent gating contributes beyond applying a fixed coefficient.

controls.name: GCAD without cropping and gating
controls.detail: Removes both components, yielding an ungated multi-layer attention-delta variant.
controls.rules_out: Tests the combined contribution of cropping and gating against multi-layer attention-delta steering without either component.

confounds.name: Long context alone causes coherence collapse
confounds.detail: The headline coherence decline under standard steering could instead be a general consequence of carrying dialogue context across turns.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper compares against system-prompt control and no-steering conditions across dialogue turns and reports that they remain comparatively stable under the same protocol.

confounds.name: GCAD’s coherence improvement comes from weakening trait steering
confounds.detail: A lower effective steering strength could preserve coherence without improving the method’s ability to express the intended trait.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper reports trait-expression scores alongside coherence, including turn-10 trait expression and average trait expression, and states that GCAD improves coherence without simply weakening steering.

confounds.name: The stability result is limited to RLHF-opposing personas
confounds.detail: The improvement could reflect behavior specific to traits opposing RLHF alignment rather than broader persona-steering stability.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper evaluates neutral traits as well and reports the same general stability trend for them.

evidence_standards.name: Repeated dialogue samples and reported variability
evidence_standards.detail: Each trait and condition uses 60 conversations from 20 question groups with 3 decoding samples per group. Main experiments run for 10 turns with the KV cache persisted, temperature 1.0, and a maximum of 500 new tokens per turn. Figures report the mean over 60 conversations with shaded ±1 standard deviation. No statistical test or seed-based significance rule is stated.

datasets.name: FLORES
datasets.eval_protocol: Used as a prospective English-to-French continuation control; the paper does not specify a split, item count, or scoring rule.

datasets.name: FEVER-derived confirmation bank
datasets.eval_protocol: Fresh bank of 1,024 confirmation rows; evaluated in three selected model-layer cells using continuous forced-choice margin and forced-choice accuracy. No split details are stated.

datasets.name: OpenBookQA
datasets.eval_protocol: Output-unseen bank of 64 facts, with a wrong-user prompt and a correct-user mirror per fact; frozen directions are evaluated on choice and continuation endpoints.

datasets.name: Anti-sycophancy audit bank
datasets.eval_protocol: 128 anti-sycophancy rows in the Qwen3-14B layer-28 audit; scored by continuous forced-choice logit contrast. The paper does not specify a named benchmark split.

metrics.name: Off-target KL (κ)
metrics.caveat: The matched budget is conditional on the neutral reference-prompt distribution, token horizon, and model setting.

metrics.name: Mean forced-choice logit-contrast change (Δb)
metrics.caveat: A mean result can conceal poor effects in the protected lower tail; the paper reports a separate tail statistic.

metrics.name: Protected-tail statistic (z₇)
metrics.caveat: Its power against alternatives is uncalibrated; the implant ladder calibrates only the mean component.

metrics.name: Forced-choice accuracy
metrics.caveat: The paper describes accuracy as a thresholded view of the same margin, not an independent endpoint.

metrics.name: Signed cosine with the observed direction
metrics.caveat: Alignment overlap describes comparator geometry; by itself it neither invalidates exchangeability nor establishes randomization invalidity.

metrics.name: Construction diagnostic A
metrics.caveat: It is an alignment-concentration diagnostic, not a validity threshold; the approximation may degrade when pair-contrast norms vary strongly.

metrics.name: Spearman correlation between cosine and measured effect
metrics.caveat: Cosine was observed rather than assigned, so the association is descriptive, not causal; pooled families also differ in more than alignment.

metrics.name: D₉₅
metrics.caveat: After the alignment-leakage analysis, it should be read as construction information retained by the sign-randomized reference relative to the isotropic reference, not as standalone efficacy or randomization validity.

metrics.name: Krippendorff’s α
metrics.caveat: Alpha is undefined for zero-variance dimensions.

metrics.name: Class-macro F1 for the automatic judge
metrics.caveat: The judge fails the paper’s calibration criteria, so judge-wide O3/O4 results are descriptive rather than confirmatory.

controls.name: Matched-KL isotropic random directions
controls.detail: Scale-normalized isotropic directions are individually tuned to the same off-target KL budget as the observed direction.
controls.rules_out: That the observed effect is explained by an arbitrary perturbation in the near-orthogonal geometric region; it does not establish uniqueness against more aligned directions.

controls.name: Matched-KL PCA-subspace directions
controls.detail: Random directions are drawn within the top-eight activation PCA subspace and matched to the same off-target KL budget.
controls.rules_out: That the effect is explained solely by drawing a direction from the dominant activation subspace.

controls.name: Matched-KL sign-randomized directions
controls.detail: Paired contrasts are independently sign-randomized while preserving paired rows, activation geometry, estimator, and scale; the prospective design also uses a separately frozen balanced block-Rademacher family.
controls.rules_out: Conditionally tests whether coherent label association is needed beyond the preserved construction, under within-pair sign exchangeability; retained target alignment limits what the comparison distinguishes.

controls.name: Exact negation of the observed direction
controls.detail: The same frozen direction is applied with its sign reversed.
controls.rules_out: A direction-insensitive generic perturbation account, insofar as the opposite direction reverses the measured effect.

controls.name: Unsteered base-model reference
controls.detail: Intervention effects are reported as observed minus base score.
controls.rules_out: That the reported score change was already present without applying the steering intervention.

controls.name: Wrong-user and correct-user polarity mirrors
controls.detail: The same facts are presented with a wrong-user prompt and a correct-user mirror.
controls.rules_out: That improved scores under wrong-user prompts necessarily reflect factual correction rather than generic opposition to the user.

controls.name: FLORES language positive control
controls.detail: A prespecified English-to-French continuation control is evaluated with the complete gate.
controls.rules_out: That a complete-gate pass is impossible under the matched-KL protocol.

controls.name: Copy-controlled Detox comparator
controls.detail: A prespecified detox comparator is evaluated alongside the language control in the prospective cells.
controls.rules_out: Categorical separation of the language control from the comparator; the paper notes that the comparator itself passes in DeepSeek.

confounds.name: The sign-randomized comparator retains target-direction alignment
confounds.detail: A strong result against a purportedly unrelated comparator could be misleading if randomized directions remain aligned with the observed direction and therefore retain its effect.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper measures each draw’s signed cosine, the empirical cosine distribution, diagnostic A, and the alignment-effect association. It concludes that this narrows comparator discriminability but does not by itself invalidate the conditional randomization test.

confounds.name: Generic opposition to the user rather than factual correction
confounds.detail: A higher score on wrong-user prompts could arise from opposing the user regardless of whether the user is wrong.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Polarity-mirrored wrong-user and correct-user evaluations, with the frozen noninferiority margin on correct-user performance; the paper finds this pattern consistent with generic opposition in several cells.

confounds.name: Nonexchangeability of within-pair signs
confounds.detail: If within-pair orientation is not exchangeable, the sign-randomization inference may not be valid even if the measured effect is large.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not empirically ruled out; the paper states that randomization validity remains conditional on within-pair sign exchangeability.

confounds.name: Automatic-judge error rather than semantic steering effect
confounds.detail: Judge-wide semantic conclusions could reflect a poorly calibrated judge rather than model behaviour.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Three-rater human-core evaluation and judge calibration checks; the judge fails calibration (class-macro F1 .562, below the stated .80 criterion), so judge-wide results are descriptive.

evidence_standards.name: Confirmatory Qwen specificity gate
evidence_standards.detail: Uses B=320 draws per null family and a preregistered intersection–union gate: both mean and protected-tail components must pass Holm-corrected α=.01 against each family. The protected-tail statistic is the seventh-smallest of 128 item effects. A non-pass is not treated as equivalence to the null.

evidence_standards.name: Prospective complete-gate tests
evidence_standards.detail: Each model-behaviour cell is tested separately with a strict Holm α<.01 complete IUT against isotropic, PCA-subspace, and separately frozen balanced block-Rademacher nulls; the design uses B=999 Monte Carlo draws. Models and behaviours are not pooled.

evidence_standards.name: Independent-bank confidence bounds
evidence_standards.detail: Transfer results report 99% lower confidence bounds; cells are not pooled.

evidence_standards.name: Human evaluation
evidence_standards.detail: Three independent raters; 768 direct-arm and 600 stratified-null rows, yielding 4,104 response ratings. Human-core tests use one-sided 99% lower bounds and the stated O1/O2 criteria.

evidence_standards.name: Open-generation decoding limit
evidence_standards.detail: The frozen output cap is 64 tokens; the paper reports that it saturates 99.996% of Qwen and 97.736% of DeepSeek outputs.

evidence_standards.name: Sensitivity analysis
evidence_standards.detail: The paper checks a conservative Γ=1.10 sensitivity envelope and reports that nominal prospective passes do not remain robust under it.

datasets.name: TruthfulQA
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate on held-out examples using closed-form multiple-choice metrics, primarily MC1. For each model-dataset-fold cell, construct the steering direction from 256 positive-negative completion pairs in a held-out direction split; use the same direction across methods. No evaluation-item count is stated.

datasets.name: SST-2
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate sentiment by the positive rate of generated continuations on held-out examples. Generate 128 tokens with nucleus sampling (p=0.95, temperature=0.7). Construct the steering direction from 256 positive-negative completion pairs in a held-out direction split; use the same direction across methods. No evaluation-item count is stated.

datasets.name: CivilComments
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate non-toxicity of generated continuations using a toxicity classifier on held-out examples. Generate 128 tokens with nucleus sampling (p=0.95, temperature=0.7). Construct the steering direction from 256 positive-negative completion pairs in a held-out direction split; use the same direction across methods. No evaluation-item count is stated.

datasets.name: IMDB
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate sentiment by the positive rate of generated continuations on held-out examples. Generate 128 tokens with nucleus sampling (p=0.95, temperature=0.7). Construct the steering direction from 256 positive-negative completion pairs in a held-out direction split; use the same direction across methods. No evaluation-item count is stated.

datasets.name: WikiText-103
datasets.eval_protocol: Compute perplexity on 200 held-out passages, with maximum length 512; report the ratio to the unsteered baseline for the same model, dataset, and fold.

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluate accuracy by log-probability ranking on a fixed subset of 300 items; used as an auxiliary measure of retained capability.

baselines.name: CAA
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses the same steering direction as the other methods within each model-dataset-fold cell and is calibrated by binary-searching its global coefficient to match the target mean achieved concept score.

baselines.name: CAA-r
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses the same steering direction and matched-mean-concept-score calibration as CAA; differs by renormalizing the additive output to the original hidden-state norm.

baselines.name: CAA-m
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses the same steering direction and is compared with S at the same per-token target concept score; the two methods have the same angular component and differ in radial behavior.

baselines.name: Spherical Steering (S)
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses the same steering direction and is compared with CAA-m at the same per-token target concept score.

baselines.name: Additive Spherical (AS)
baselines.fair_comparison: Uses the same steering direction; its global angular-displacement parameter is binary-searched to match the target mean achieved concept score.

metrics.name: Non-toxicity measured by a toxicity classifier
Coefficient of variation of hidden-state norms
Linear probe accuracy
metrics.caveat: Raw-state accuracy alone does not distinguish directional from norm-based concept information; the paper also reports probes on normalized hidden states and on scalar norms.

metrics.name: Per-token concept-score variance
metrics.caveat: Mean concept score alone does not capture the distribution of achieved scores across tokens; the paper also measures per-token score variance.

metrics.name: WikiText-103 perplexity ratio
metrics.caveat: Perplexity does not measure semantic steering or retained capability; the paper reports it alongside downstream task metrics and MMLU accuracy.

metrics.name: MMLU accuracy
metrics.caveat: Used as an auxiliary measure of retained capability, alongside perplexity and downstream task metrics.

controls.name: Unsteered model
controls.detail: The paper reports perplexity relative to the unsteered baseline for the same model, dataset, and fold, and uses an unsteered reference for capability comparisons.
controls.rules_out: Provides a reference for judging degradation associated with steering rather than attributing the steered model's absolute score to the intervention.

controls.name: CAA-r versus CAA
controls.detail: CAA-r applies the same additive update as CAA and then restores the original norm.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether post-hoc norm preservation alone explains a change in steering behavior.

controls.name: S versus CAA-m at matched per-token concept score
controls.detail: Both reach the same angular target for each token; S restores the original norm, while CAA-m allows the norm to change.
controls.rules_out: A difference in downstream stability can be attributed to radial behavior rather than a different angular target.

controls.name: CAA-r versus AS
controls.detail: Both preserve the original norm, but they produce different token-level angular profiles; their global strengths are calibrated to the same mean concept score.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether norm preservation alone explains outcomes, rather than the distribution of per-token angular effects.

controls.name: SN with beta=1 (S) versus SN at other beta values
controls.detail: Hold the angular target fixed and vary only the multiplicative norm scale; beta=1 is exactly S.
controls.rules_out: Isolates the effect of radial scaling under fixed angular control.

confounds.name: Concept information is encoded in norm rather than direction
confounds.detail: The apparent success of normalized-state probes could otherwise be mistaken for evidence about direction without testing whether magnitude carries the concept information.
confounds.ruled_out_by: For each model and concept dataset, compare linear probes on raw hidden states, normalized hidden states, and scalar norms; normalized probes closely match raw probes while norm-only probes remain near chance.

confounds.name: Differences between steering methods arise from different steering directions
confounds.detail: A method could appear better because its estimated direction differs, not because its intervention geometry differs.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Use the same contrastive mean-difference direction for all methods within each model-dataset-fold cell.

confounds.name: Differences attributed to norm are actually due to different angular control
confounds.detail: Different achieved concept scores or token-level angular profiles could explain downstream differences even if norm had no effect.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare CAA-m and S at the same per-token target score; for fixed-strength methods, calibrate to a matched mean score and measure per-token concept-score variance.

confounds.name: Norm preservation alone explains stability in fixed-strength steering
confounds.detail: The stability difference between fixed-strength methods might be due simply to whether they preserve the original norm.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Compare CAA with CAA-r and compare the norm-preserving CAA-r with AS, which has a different token-level angular profile.

confounds.name: Changing beta changes semantic steering as well as stability
confounds.detail: A perplexity improvement could reflect weaker semantic steering rather than a radial effect at fixed semantic control.
confounds.ruled_out_by: In SN, vary beta while holding gamma fixed, and report task metrics alongside perplexity; task metrics remain within about 2.5 percentage points across tested beta values.

evidence_standards.name: One seed and two folds
evidence_standards.detail: Unless otherwise stated, results are aggregated over seven models, four datasets, one seed, and two folds. The paper does not state a statistical test, confidence interval, or general threshold for treating differences as real.

evidence_standards.name: Generation decoding setting
evidence_standards.detail: Generation-based evaluations use 128 tokens with nucleus sampling at p=0.95 and temperature 0.7.

datasets.name: Persona Steering: Persona Vectors
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses the evil, sycophantic, and hallucinating traits for evaluation; apathetic and humorous are used for hyperparameter tuning. For each trait, evaluates on 20 questions and samples 10 responses per question. Generation uses temperature 1.0 and top-p 1.0. Non-prompt steering methods receive the unsteered prompts; trait presence and coherence are scored with the attribute and coherence judges. Reports scores macro-averaged over traits.

datasets.name: IFEval (augmented format and language instructions)
datasets.eval_protocol: Evaluates 12 format-instruction types and answer-in-language-X instructions for 14 languages with training and test instances. Uses the IFEval evaluation script for instruction-following accuracy and the coherence judge; reports both macro-averaged over instruction types. Steered responses use greedy decoding. For PSR and Const, the global steering coefficient is fixed at 1.

datasets.name: AxBench
datasets.eval_protocol: Uses the Gemma-2-2B-L20 and Gemma-2-9B-L20 subsets, each covering 500 target concepts. Each concept has 72 training, 5 validation, and 5 test triplets; the steered responses were generated by a frontier LLM. Uses the dataset setup and evaluation script and reports its overall steering score.

baselines.name: Prompt steering (prompt)
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated on the same benchmarks and language models; on Persona Vectors, prompt steering is also the reference coherence used for TA@Cp.

baselines.name: Stolfo et al. (2025) activation steering
baselines.fair_comparison: On IFEval, the authors reproduce the method with its code to evaluate coherence; they also report the published results as a reference. The study follows the same language-model and steering-layer setup used for the comparison.

baselines.name: Difference-in-means (DiM) activation steering
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same Persona Vectors models and task setup; single-layer steering uses the selected effective layer, and the reported DiM results use Chen et al. (2025)'s code.

baselines.name: SAE
baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2-2B-L20 and Gemma-2-9B-L20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

baselines.name: ReFT-r1
baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2 layer-20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2 layer-20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2 layer-20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

baselines.name: LoRA-RePS
baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2 layer-20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2 layer-20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

baselines.name: HyperSteer
baselines.fair_comparison: Reported as an AxBench reference on the same Gemma-2 layer-20 subsets and steering-score evaluation.

metrics.name: TA@C80 (trait alignment at coherence 80.0)
metrics.caveat: Trait alignment can be affected by coherence and oversteering; the paper reports alignment at a fixed coherence level and also at prompt-steering coherence.

metrics.name: TA@Cp (trait alignment at prompt-steering coherence)
metrics.caveat: Trait alignment comparisons can be affected by coherence differences; this reports alignment at the average coherence of prompt steering, alongside TA@C80.

metrics.name: IFEval instruction-following accuracy (IF Acc.)
metrics.caveat: Accuracy alone does not show coherence costs; the paper reports coherence alongside it.

metrics.name: AxBench overall steering score
metrics.caveat: The aggregate combines concept presence, fluency, and answer relevance and can conceal a drop in an individual dimension; the paper reports dimension breakdowns and notes a noticeable answer-relevance drop for A-PSRMSE on the 2B subset.

metrics.name: Relative RMSE between prompt-steering and method interventions
metrics.caveat: A relative RMSE of 1 corresponds to the faithfulness of a forward pass without steering; the paper also compares against equivalent trait-eliciting prompts as a reference.

controls.name: No steering
controls.detail: Evaluates the model without an activation intervention or steering instruction in the prompt where the no-steering reference is reported.
controls.rules_out: Whether the observed behavior is already present without steering.

controls.name: Constant activation steering (S-Const/A-Const)
controls.detail: Compares constant-coefficient steering with PSR under the single-layer and all-layer settings; the paper also compares corresponding training objectives and intervention positions.
controls.rules_out: Whether gains require PSR's token-specific steering coefficients rather than activation steering with a constant coefficient.

confounds.name: Higher trait alignment could come from lower-coherence or oversteered completions
confounds.detail: A steering method could appear to improve trait alignment while producing less coherent responses or by steering more aggressively.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Reports trait alignment at fixed coherence 80.0 and at prompt-steering coherence, and reports coherence alongside trait alignment.

confounds.name: AxBench aggregate gains could mask worse answer relevance
confounds.detail: An improved overall steering score could result despite a decline in relevance to the base prompt.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Breaks down the AxBench score into concept alignment, fluency, and answer relevance; the paper explicitly notes the relevance drop for A-PSRMSE on the 2B subset.

confounds.name: Intervention faithfulness could depend on the particular trait-eliciting prompt wording
confounds.detail: A method could appear faithful to one prompt-steering intervention simply because the reference instruction has a particular wording.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Reports relative RMSE against prompt steering using different but equivalent trait-eliciting instructions as a reference.

evidence_standards.name: Persona Vectors decoding
evidence_standards.detail: Reports generations sampled with temperature 1.0 and top-p 1.0; 10 responses are sampled per evaluation question.

evidence_standards.name: IFEval decoding
evidence_standards.detail: Reports steered responses generated with greedy decoding.

baselines.name: Published gain estimator (single-dose ratio and AUC-over-doses ratio)
baselines.fair_comparison: Reconstructed from the released analysis code and applied to this paper’s swept-grid rollouts; recomputed per-dose effects reproduce the committed records exactly.

baselines.name: Vertical rescaling
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with horizontal reparametrization at equal model complexity on the same frozen five-cell roster.

baselines.name: Intercept-only predictor
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated in the same leave-one-family-out, four-family head-to-head set, with no per-model fitted parameter.

baselines.name: A_lin (training-free logit-lens accuracy)
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated in the same leave-one-family-out, four-family head-to-head set.

baselines.name: Perturbation sensitivity λ
baselines.fair_comparison: Evaluated in the same leave-one-family-out, four-family head-to-head set.

metrics.name: Length-controlled combined binary
metrics.caveat: The paper’s errata say it is length-correlated: it holds on the field it names, not on the property its name asserts.

metrics.name: dEC₅₀
metrics.caveat: A location at response level 0.5, not evidence that the curves are translates; raw dose units are model-specific. The paper reports Λ as a dose-unit-free companion and tests other response levels, links, and fit windows.

metrics.name: Λ (log-potency displacement)
metrics.caveat: It supports cross-family comparisons on a dose-unit-free scale, but does not establish a common curve form; the paper reports that fitted dEC₅₀ varies across links.

metrics.name: Gain ratio T
metrics.caveat: A ratio at an operating point does not identify potency and efficacy, moves with dose, and its point and AUC forms can disagree. The paper reports swept curves and dEC₅₀ alongside it.

metrics.name: Fitted upper asymptote
metrics.caveat: Agreement in asymptotes does not establish equal achievable effect; on a bypass cell the asymptote is at the refusal floor and can be blind to how much refusal was removed. The paper reports coherent/deliverable contrasts alongside it.

metrics.name: Coherence fraction h(α) / coherent margin
metrics.caveat: Coherence is an outcome, not a basis for excluding a cell; the paper separately applies the α* validity screen and quarantines the cell whose response inverts after coherence collapse.

metrics.name: ΔAIC for horizontal versus vertical fit
metrics.caveat: A preference for horizontal reparametrization does not mean the curves are translates; the paper also reports the displacement difference across response levels, Δq.

metrics.name: LOFO MAE and R²_pred
metrics.caveat: The head-to-head set has only four families; sign accuracy is not discriminating because all are negative-signed, and the reported predictor result is gauge-bound. The paper reports the held-out Gemma result separately and refutes its registered prediction.

controls.name: Matched-norm random directions
controls.detail: At least five matched-norm random directions per cell; used in the per-dose Δ(real)−Δ(random) diagnostic and as an admission gate, not subtracted from the fitted response.
controls.rules_out: That the observed effect is explained by an equally norm-sized random intervention.

controls.name: Matched-information template ladder (C0 to C3)
controls.detail: Compares chat (C0) with a ReAct scaffold using deterministic dummy tools (C3), matched on instruction; the paper notes the directive is asymmetric between them.
controls.rules_out: Whether the context/template change is accompanied by a change in task instruction or information, subject to the stated directive asymmetry.

controls.name: Full KV recomputation at every agent turn
controls.detail: Every agent rollout recomputes the full KV state at each turn; the implementation is structurally verified in both agent code paths.
controls.rules_out: That the reported result depends on KV-cache reuse or contamination.

controls.name: Reciprocal extraction frame
controls.detail: A pre-registered sensitivity analysis also extracts the direction inside the agent frame and compares it with the chat-extracted direction; it uses a non-canonical parser metric, four agent turns, and one or two real doses, rather than refitting dEC₅₀.
controls.rules_out: That the observed sign is solely an artifact of using a chat-native direction; the test is limited to one model and does not establish extraction invariance.

confounds.name: Residual-norm rescaling
confounds.detail: Different residual norms could make the same commanded α a different relative perturbation and shift the midpoint without a context-dependent steering mechanism.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure the agent/chat residual-norm ratio and compare its sign pattern with Λ: log ρ is negative in all five cells, while Λ has both signs; on the positive Llama cell the predicted sign is opposite.

confounds.name: Baseline alignment
confounds.detail: A context-dependent unsteered residual component along the steering direction could create an apparent potency shift as an offset.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure the baseline cosine and test the resulting composed scale-plus-translation law; it is rejected in three of five scorable cells, predicts the wrong sign on the positive cell, and dividing out the drive increases rather than removes that displacement.

confounds.name: Dose transduction
confounds.detail: A commanded steering unit may produce a different residual displacement in the longer ReAct prompt than in chat, creating an apparent shift in commanded-dose units.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Measure delivered displacement per commanded unit and test its predicted shift: it predicts the opposite sign in two of three cells and explains only 3.0% of the shift where its sign agrees. Re-expression in chat-delivered units preserves sign and CI-exclusion in all three measured cells.

confounds.name: KV-cache contamination
confounds.detail: Multi-turn coherence failure or the measured transfer effect could arise from reusing contaminated KV state rather than from the claimed context-dependent response.
confounds.ruled_out_by: All agent rollouts use verified full KV recomputation at every turn, so cache reuse is absent by construction; the paper limits this conclusion to its protocol.

confounds.name: Chat-native direction / extraction-frame dependence
confounds.detail: Because the steering direction was extracted in chat, the result might not transport to a direction extracted in the agent frame.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Run the reciprocal-extraction-frame sensitivity analysis. All 20 admissible cells have the canonical negative sign and exclude zero, with a maximum frame ratio below the registered 2.0 bound; the paper limits the inference to one model and does not claim extraction invariance.

confounds.name: Coherence-collapse fit artifact
confounds.detail: A response inversion after coherence collapse can flip a fitted curve’s orientation and manufacture a large apparent midpoint shift.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Apply the α* screen, report coherence as an outcome, and quarantine OLMo-2-7B:induce: its fitted midpoint and observed-crossing summaries have opposite signs, and it is excluded from law claims.

evidence_standards.name: Item-paired bootstrap uncertainty
evidence_standards.detail: Use B=10,000 item-paired bootstrap resamples and report 95% confidence intervals; the paper describes CI-exclusion of zero as CI-clear for the primary displacement results.

evidence_standards.name: Decoding setting
evidence_standards.detail: Results use greedy decoding.

evidence_standards.name: α* validity screen
evidence_standards.detail: A cell contributes to law claims only when both fitted midpoints are below the empirically determined dose at which real-direction cross-context separation collapses into the matched-norm random band; α*-RED cells are reported but excluded.

evidence_standards.name: Horizontal-versus-vertical fit comparison
evidence_standards.detail: At equal model complexity, the frozen five-cell audit counts a win when the ΔAIC interval excludes zero; the registered α*-trimmed secondary is reported separately as four of five.

evidence_standards.name: Heterogeneity and power
evidence_standards.detail: The registered specification uses the model as the unit, α*-GREEN cells only, and reports Q, I², τ and joint sign power; τ is compared with a design minimum of 2.653.

datasets.name: Curated object-level “explain how” prompt set
datasets.eval_protocol: 38 prompts spanning topics including math, basic business skills, and housekeeping. The paper evaluates steered responses with a judge that splits attempts at explicit verbal self-correction and scores each attempt 0–100 for addressing the prompt while avoiding the steering topic. Main model trial counts are Llama-3.3-70B: 4,877; Llama-3.1-8B: 4,512; Gemma-2-27B: 4,914; Gemma-2-9B: 4,668; Gemma-2-2B: 4,948. In the boost sweep, 10 levels from threshold−3σ to threshold+3σ were tested, with about 226 responses per level.

datasets.name: Disjoint held-out prompt set
datasets.eval_protocol: 20 prompts spanning five new domains, used to validate the latent-ablation effect; the paper reports 5.0% baseline ESR and a 30–45% reduction under ablation.

baselines.name: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the curated prompt set using its corresponding SAE and steering at a similar relative model depth. Steering thresholds were calibrated per latent to yield a first-attempt judge score of 30/100.

baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the curated prompt set using its corresponding SAE and steering at a similar relative model depth. Steering thresholds were calibrated per latent to yield a first-attempt judge score of 30/100.

baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the curated prompt set using its corresponding SAE and steering at a similar relative model depth. Steering thresholds were calibrated per latent to yield a first-attempt judge score of 30/100.

baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the curated prompt set using its corresponding SAE and steering at a similar relative model depth. Steering thresholds were calibrated per latent to yield a first-attempt judge score of 30/100.

metrics.name: Multi-attempt rate
metrics.caveat: Counts responses with at least two attempts marked by explicit verbal restarts; it does not establish that a correction succeeds. Reported alongside conditional improvement rate and ESR rate.

metrics.name: Conditional improvement rate
metrics.caveat: Measures improvement only among multi-attempt responses, so it does not show how often the model attempts to correct. Reported alongside multi-attempt rate and ESR rate.

metrics.name: ESR rate
metrics.caveat: Requires an explicit verbal restart and an improved final attempt, so implicit or non-verbalized recovery is not captured. Reported alongside multi-attempt rate and conditional improvement rate.

metrics.name: First-attempt score
metrics.caveat: Used to calibrate steering strength; the paper also compares it across conditions to check whether initial response quality changed.

metrics.name: Judge score (0–100)
metrics.caveat: Scores relevance while avoiding the steering topic. In the matched-prefix experiment, continuation scores use a simple relevance judge and are explicitly not directly comparable to the 0–100 scores elsewhere.

controls.name: Unsteered responses
controls.detail: The same task prompts are answered without a steering intervention; the paper reports 7,892 such trials.
controls.rules_out: That the observed self-correction simply reflects spontaneous baseline behavior in the absence of steering.

controls.name: Random-latent ablation
controls.detail: Random latents matched to the targeted latents for activation frequency and magnitude are ablated.
controls.rules_out: That ablating any similarly active latents would produce the reduction in self-correction.

controls.name: Unsteered prefilling
controls.detail: The first 500, 1,100, 1,500, or 2,000 characters of a steered episode are prefixed to a fresh, unsteered assistant response, which is then continued and judged.
controls.rules_out: Tests whether off-topic text alone can elicit a restart, without ongoing steering.

controls.name: Matched on-topic prefix followed by steered continuation
controls.detail: A clean, unsteered on-topic prefix, length-matched to the natural post-correction segment, is followed by a steered continuation; a steered no-prefix condition is also measured.
controls.rules_out: Tests how much sustained on-topic continuation can be explained by recent on-topic text alone, relative to natural post-correction text under steering.

controls.name: Held-out prompts under latent ablation
controls.detail: The targeted ablation is tested on a disjoint set of 20 prompts across five new domains.
controls.rules_out: That the ablation result is specific to the prompts used to discover the latents.

confounds.name: The restart is text-conditioned rather than evidence of an internal monitor
confounds.detail: If reading its own off-topic text is sufficient, the restart could occur without monitoring the active steering perturbation.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out; the prefilling control supports this account for the restart itself: an unsteered model given an off-topic prefix self-corrects more often than the steered model.

confounds.name: Autoregressive conditioning on recent on-topic tokens explains sustained resistance
confounds.detail: The model might stay on-topic after a correction simply because its recent context is on-topic.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The matched-prefix experiment finds that a length-matched on-topic prefix improves continuation scores, but natural post-correction text improves them 2.1 times more (p<0.001). The paper concludes that autoregressive conditioning explains roughly half, not all, of the post-correction quality.

confounds.name: The matched-prefix residual reflects richer corrective text rather than a resistance mechanism
confounds.detail: The specific corrective phrasing may provide stronger context than a generic on-topic prefix; the paper also considers recruitment of downstream mechanisms or use of steering as information.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not resolved by the paper; the matched-prefix experiment establishes that the generic length-matched prefix is insufficient but does not distinguish among these remaining accounts.

confounds.name: The latent-ablation effect is a generic consequence of ablating active latents
confounds.detail: Ablating latents could reduce ESR regardless of whether the selected latents are specifically associated with self-correction.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Random latents matched for activation frequency and magnitude produce no reduction; the paper also reports that targeted ablation leaves mean first-attempt score similar.

confounds.name: The latent-ablation result is an artifact of the discovery prompts
confounds.detail: The candidate latents were identified using the evaluation prompts, so their apparent effect might not generalize beyond those prompts.
confounds.ruled_out_by: On a disjoint set of 20 prompts across five new domains, baseline ESR is 5.0% and targeted ablation reduces it by 30–45%.

confounds.name: The effect is specific to SAE-derived steering
confounds.detail: The observed resistance could depend on the SAE steering representation rather than applying to another steering-vector source.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper reports a comparable 3.6% ESR rate using Wikipedia-derived contrastive vectors on Llama-3.3-70B.

confounds.name: Meta-prompting elicits restart language without installing or recruiting monitoring
confounds.detail: The increase could reflect bias toward a generative pattern of emitting restart phrases, rather than a monitoring process.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not ruled out. The paper notes that first-attempt scores remain similar and conditional improvement is similar while attempts increase, and explicitly says this pattern is consistent with generative bias.

confounds.name: Model scale, architecture, or training explains cross-model differences
confounds.detail: The higher explicit ESR in Llama-3.3-70B might reflect architecture or training differences rather than scale.
confounds.ruled_out_by: Not disentangled; the paper compares five models across the Llama-3 and Gemma-2 families and explicitly acknowledges that scale, architecture, and training cannot be separated.

confounds.name: Fine-tuning increases surface imitation without improving effective correction
confounds.detail: More self-correction training examples could teach restart behavior without improving the ability to correct under continued steering; alternatively, steering could cap post-correction quality.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The fine-tuning experiment measures multi-attempt rate and conditional improvement across training-data ratios: attempts rise while conditional improvement remains flat. The paper treats the two explanations as unresolved.

evidence_standards.name: Uncertainty intervals and reported significance
evidence_standards.detail: Figures report 95% confidence intervals: binomial standard errors for percentages and standard errors of the mean for score improvement. The matched-prefix comparison reports p<0.001, but the statistical test is not specified in the provided text. No seed count or seed-level variance procedure is stated; generation uses a repetition penalty, but its decoding settings are not specified here.

datasets.name: Six fixed evaluation contexts (Ambiguous, Coding, Document, Emotional support, Creative, Borderline-harmful)
datasets.eval_protocol: 16 prompts per context (96 total under full coverage); cross-effects are estimated by pooling the contexts. The borderline-harmful set includes dual-use and benign prompts testing under- and over-refusal.

datasets.name: XSTest
datasets.eval_protocol: Prompts adapted from the safe half of XSTest are incorporated into the borderline-harmful prompt set; XSTest is not reported as a separate evaluation.

baselines.name: Rubric-text similarity
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the new-source held-out split using mean Spearman correlation; the paper reports it only for this split.

baselines.name: Raw cosine similarity
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same new-source and new-target held-out splits using mean Spearman correlation.

baselines.name: Whitened cosine similarity
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same new-source and new-target held-out splits using mean Spearman correlation.

baselines.name: Direct probe
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same new-source and new-target held-out splits; it removes the propagation map and scores the source direction against the target probe.

baselines.name: Per-target mean
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same held-out splits using mean Spearman correlation; uses the measured cross-effect matrix.

baselines.name: Nearest-neighbor transfer
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same held-out splits using mean Spearman correlation; copies a profile from an already measured behavior.

baselines.name: Measured-shift readout
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared on the same held-out splits using mean Spearman correlation; runs the steering intervention and reads the observed activation shift with the behavioral probes.

baselines.name: Majority-sign baseline
baselines.fair_comparison: Compared with the forecaster’s sign predictions on the top decile of predicted side effects.

metrics.name: Mean Spearman rank correlation
metrics.caveat: Judge scores are ordinal rather than interval-scaled, and relative ordering of side effects is more reproducible than absolute magnitudes; the paper therefore evaluates ranked profiles.

metrics.name: Sign accuracy
metrics.caveat: Reported for the top decile of predicted side effects; the paper compares it with the majority-sign baseline.

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.caveat: Used to filter target behaviors by probe quality (at least 0.76 in at least five of six contexts); no further caveat is stated.

metrics.name: Judged behavior score
metrics.caveat: Scores are ordinal on a 1–4 scale; the paper uses relative ranking rather than treating score differences as interval-scaled for forecasting evaluation.

metrics.name: Cross-effect coupling / total score change
metrics.caveat: Raw slopes are not directly comparable across behaviors because steering ranges differ; the paper reports total score change across each source behavior’s calibrated steering window and compares effect sizes only within a model.

metrics.name: Variance explained
metrics.caveat: No general caveat is stated; the paper also checks the dominant mode on unsteered generations and measures response-length contribution.

metrics.name: Participation ratio (effective dimensionality)
metrics.caveat: The paper compares the measured matrix’s participation ratio with shuffled controls.

metrics.name: Spearman agreement between judges
metrics.caveat: Agreement indicates consistency between judges, not absolute ground truth; the authors explicitly note that their results establish consistency under the judges rather than ground truth.

controls.name: Random steering directions
controls.detail: The paper applies random steering directions and measures judged-score changes; these change scores by about 0.007.
controls.rules_out: That observed side effects are produced merely by applying an arbitrary steering direction.

controls.name: Shuffled controls for intrinsic dimensionality
controls.detail: The paper compares the measured matrix’s participation ratio (4.6–4.9) with shuffled controls (23–26); the specific shuffling procedure is not given in the provided text.
controls.rules_out: That the low effective dimensionality is also present in shuffled data.

controls.name: Unsteered generations
controls.detail: The same behaviors are evaluated on unsteered generations; the dominant mode explains 8.6–10.0% of variance there, and response length accounts for at most 19% of measured couplings.
controls.rules_out: That the observed structure is simply an artifact of the behavior taxonomy, judge, or response length rather than an interaction introduced by steering.

confounds.name: Measured side effects are measurement noise rather than genuine behavioral interactions
confounds.detail: The cross-effect matrix could reflect variation in prompt-level slopes rather than reliable steering effects.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper uses two-sided t-tests with Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q<0.05 across off-diagonal entries, treats nonsignificant entries as zero, and reports split-half matrix Spearman correlations of 0.73–0.86. It also reports a detectable-coupling floor of 0.10–0.12 versus a median significant coupling about twice that size.

confounds.name: The measured structure is an artifact of the taxonomy, judge, or response length rather than steering
confounds.detail: The same apparent structure could arise from how behaviors are defined or scored, or from changes in response length.
confounds.ruled_out_by: On unsteered generations the dominant mode explains only 8.6–10.0% of variance, and response length accounts for at most 19% of measured couplings; a second judge agrees with the primary judge at Spearman 0.93 on re-rated scores.

confounds.name: Side effects are caused by degenerate outputs at excessive steering strengths
confounds.detail: A steering intervention could make outputs degenerate, so score changes might not represent meaningful behavioral changes.
confounds.ruled_out_by: For each validated source, the paper calibrates the widest steering-coefficient window whose generations remain free of degeneration and measures effects within that window.

confounds.name: Asymmetric effects are driven by a small number of outliers
confounds.detail: Opposite-signed effects for steering A toward B versus B toward A could be due to a few anomalous pairs.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper reports additional re-testing of asymmetric interactions and says the results are robust rather than driven by a small number of outliers.

confounds.name: The forecaster’s held-out performance comes from leakage of measured side effects
confounds.detail: A forecast could appear accurate if held-out cross-effects influenced training or model selection.
confounds.ruled_out_by: The paper uses source-held-out and target-held-out splits, holds out each behavior once, and selects the ridge regularization strength using nested cross-validation on training behaviors only.

evidence_standards.name: Cross-effect significance
evidence_standards.detail: For each matrix entry, the paper uses a two-sided t-test based on per-prompt slopes and a Student’s t distribution with P−1 degrees of freedom; significance requires Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q<0.05 across all off-diagonal entries for that model. Nonsignificant entries are treated as zero.

evidence_standards.name: Forecast comparison significance
evidence_standards.detail: Differences between propagation and raw cosine are assessed with a paired cluster bootstrap; the paper marks significant splits in its results table.

evidence_standards.name: Measurement reproducibility
evidence_standards.detail: The paper reconstructs the cross-effect matrix from two disjoint prompt subsets and reports Spearman correlations of 0.73–0.86.

evidence_standards.name: Judge agreement
evidence_standards.detail: A second judge re-scores a confirmation subset; agreement with the primary judge is reported as Spearman 0.93 on re-rated individual scores.

evidence_standards.name: Generation sampling
evidence_standards.detail: For each steering coefficient, the paper generates four independent samples; it sweeps five evenly spaced coefficients within the calibrated steering window.
